column1: # JoyPro's own names and explanations of the IL-2 Korea actions (written for JoyPro, not copied from the game).
# The name is shown when the game gives the action no text of its own; the category is the section of the
# game's Key Mapping menu; the explanation is the "what it does" line of the catalog, search and relation editor.

column4: explanation
Saves a picture of the current screen. Use it to keep a moment of the flight.
Stops and resumes the simulation (single player). Use it to take a break or look at the cockpit at rest.
Speeds up mission time, for example on a long flight to the target. Press again for more speed.
Slows mission time down again, back to normal or slower than real time.
Starts or stops recording the flight as a track you can replay and film later.
Shows or hides the frames-per-second counter, to check how smoothly the game runs.
Opens or closes the in-game menu (settings, leave the mission).
Shows the mission state and the list of players on the server.
Shows or hides the briefing map with the task, the route and your notes.
Steps to the next mode of the mini-map in the HUD.
Switches between the sets of HUD instruments (none, basic, full).
Shows or hides the HUD markers and the aiming help.
Opens the chat line to write a message to the other players.
Hides or shows the whole HUD, for a clean view or screenshots.
Opens the command menu for orders to your flight and radio messages.
For VR headsets with a fixed lens distance: shifts the VR image a step outwards so it fits your eyes.
For VR headsets with a fixed lens distance: shifts the VR image a step inwards so it fits your eyes.
Puts the view back to its default angle and distance.
Makes the free camera move slowly, for precise positioning (replays, screenshots). Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
Zooms the external camera in and out. Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
Turns the external camera up and down around the object it shows.
Turns the external camera left and right around the object it shows.
Turns the external camera up and down on the spot, without circling the object.
Turns the external camera left and right on the spot, without circling the object.
Moves the free camera forward and backward. Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
Moves the free camera sideways. Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
Moves the free camera up and down. Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
Switches back to your own cockpit view. This is the normal flying view.
Switches to the automatic director camera that shows the action from the enemy side.
Switches to the automatic director camera that shows the action from your own side.
Locks the view on a friendly aircraft, so the camera keeps it in the picture. Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
Locks the view on an enemy aircraft, so the camera keeps it in the picture. Press again for the next one. Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
Locks the view on the enemy aircraft that is the biggest threat to you right now. Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
Locks the view on a friendly ground unit. Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
Locks the view on an enemy ground unit, for example a target you attack. Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
Switches to a camera that follows the current object from behind and keeps its target in view.
Switches to the free external camera around your own aircraft. Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
Switches to the external camera on a friendly aircraft. Press again for the next one. Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
Switches to the external camera on an enemy aircraft. Press again for the next one. Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
Switches to the external camera on a ground unit. Press again for the next one. Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
Switches to the external camera on a friendly ground unit. Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
Switches to the external camera on an enemy ground unit. Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
Follows a bomb or rocket in flight, to see where it hits. Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
Follows a bomb or rocket dropped by your side. Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
Follows a bomb or rocket dropped by the enemy. Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
A fixed camera the current object flies past, like a spectator on the ground. Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
Detaches the camera so you can fly it anywhere with the free camera controls.
Switches through the cameras attached to the aircraft (wing, tail, gear).
In a replay: shows the flight with the camera as it was recorded.
In a replay: a cockpit camera you can turn freely.
While held, the mouse turns your view instead of steering, so you can look around and keep flying.
Zooms the cockpit view in and out with an axis. Zoom in to spot and identify far aircraft.
Zooms the cockpit view in, step by step, to see far things larger. Handy on buttons for quick looks at far targets.
Zooms the cockpit view out, step by step, for a wider field of view. Handy on buttons for quick looks at far targets.
Sets the cockpit zoom back to normal. Handy on buttons for quick looks at far targets.
Jumps straight to the widest cockpit view (least zoom). Handy on buttons for quick looks at far targets.
Jumps straight to cockpit zoom step 1. Handy on buttons for quick looks at far targets.
Jumps straight to cockpit zoom step 2. Handy on buttons for quick looks at far targets.
Jumps straight to cockpit zoom step 3. Handy on buttons for quick looks at far targets.
Jumps straight to the strongest cockpit zoom. Handy on buttons for quick looks at far targets.
Zooms the view while you aim a turret with the mouse (the game calls it turret zoom).
Zooms the view in the game's Mouse control mode (the mouse steers, see "Mouse control: flight direction").
Moves your head view up and down with an axis (normally the mouse; a mini stick or head tracking works too).
Turns your head view left and right with an axis (normally the mouse; a mini stick or head tracking works too).
Turns the view of a gunner position left and right with an axis; it can go all the way round.
Changes how the view buttons move your head: panning, centred, fixed or gradual.

column2: Save head position as snap view
column4: Stores where your head is now as the snap position of the current view button.
Hold it together with a snap view button to look to that side and up.
Hold it together with a snap view button to look to that side and down.
Hold it together with a snap view button to use the head position you saved for it.
Turns your head view up (or snaps to look forward, depending on the view mode). Good on a hat switch.
Turns your head view up-right (or snaps to look forward right, depending on the view mode). Good on a hat switch.
Turns your head view right (or snaps to look right, depending on the view mode). Good on a hat switch.
Turns your head view down-right (or snaps to look back right, depending on the view mode). Good on a hat switch.
Turns your head view down (or snaps to look back, depending on the view mode). Good on a hat switch.
Turns your head view down-left (or snaps to look back left, depending on the view mode). Good on a hat switch.
Turns your head view left (or snaps to look left, depending on the view mode). Good on a hat switch.
Turns your head view up-left (or snaps to look forward left, depending on the view mode). Good on a hat switch.
Turns the vision block of the vehicle position you are in.
Moves your head in the cockpit forward, for example to see past the gunsight or the canopy frame.
Moves your head in the cockpit back, for example to see past the gunsight or the canopy frame.
Moves your head in the cockpit left, for example to see past the gunsight or the canopy frame.
Moves your head in the cockpit right, for example to see past the gunsight or the canopy frame.
Moves your head in the cockpit up, for example to see past the gunsight or the canopy frame.
Moves your head in the cockpit down, for example to see past the gunsight or the canopy frame.
Moves your view up and down while you look through a turret gunsight, without moving the gun.
Moves your view left and right while you look through a turret gunsight, without moving the gun.
Turns the dynamic cockpit view right and left with an axis (normally the mouse).
Turns the dynamic cockpit view down and up with an axis (normally the mouse).
Hands the aircraft to the computer pilot, which flies the route for you. Press again to take over.
The computer holds the aircraft in level flight while you look around or navigate.
While a flight helper holds the aircraft, steers it into a gentle left turn.
While a flight helper holds the aircraft, steers it into a gentle right turn.
Moves the elevator: nose up or down. Put it on the forward/back axis of your stick.
Moves the ailerons: rolls the aircraft left or right. Put it on the left/right axis of your stick.
Moves the rudder: turns the nose left or right, for coordinated turns, take-off and landing. Put it on pedals or a twist axis.
Puts the rudder back to the middle when you steer the rudder with buttons.
Sets the rudder trim with an axis, so the aircraft flies straight without pressing the pedal.
Trims the rudder a step to the left. Use it to stop the nose drifting right.
Trims the rudder a step to the right. Use it to stop the nose drifting left.
Sets the elevator trim with an axis, so the aircraft holds its pitch without pressure on the stick.
Trims the elevator a step nose up. Use it when you keep pulling the stick to hold height.
Trims the elevator a step nose down. Use it when you keep pushing the stick, for example at high speed.
Sets the aileron trim with an axis, so the wings stay level without pressure on the stick.
Trims the ailerons a step to the left, when a wing keeps dropping to the right.
Trims the ailerons a step to the right, when a wing keeps dropping to the left.
Sets every trim back to neutral, for example after a fight or before landing.
Moves the adjustable stabiliser with an axis (aircraft that trim pitch this way).
Moves the adjustable stabiliser a step nose up, when you keep pulling the stick.
Moves the adjustable stabiliser a step nose down, when you keep pushing the stick at high speed.
Retracts the flaps a step. Raise them after take-off as speed builds.
Extends the flaps a step, for more lift at low speed: take-off and landing.
Extends or retracts the air brakes, to slow down quickly or keep the speed down in a dive.
Extends the air brakes, to slow down quickly or keep the speed down in a dive. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Retracts the air brakes again when you want your speed back. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Switches the dive siren on or off; it howls while you dive on a target.
Switches the dive siren on. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Switches the dive siren off. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Switches the windscreen wipers on or off, where the aircraft has them.
Arms the automatic dive recovery that pulls the aircraft out of a dive bombing attack.
Raises or lowers the landing gear. Raise it after take-off, lower it before landing.
Raises the landing gear. Do it right after take-off, once you climb away, to lose the drag.
Lowers the landing gear. Do it on the approach, before landing.
Locks or frees the tail (or nose) wheel. Lock it for take-off and landing, free it to taxi in tight turns.
Locks the tail (or nose) wheel straight. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Frees the tail (or nose) wheel so it can swivel. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Brakes both main wheels with an axis or button; with the rudder deflected it brakes one side to steer on the ground.
Brakes the left main wheel (toe brake of the left pedal).
Brakes the right main wheel (toe brake of the right pedal).
Brakes the nose or tail wheel, where the aircraft has a brake there.
Sets or releases the parking brake that holds the aircraft still on the ground.
Sets the parking brake. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Releases the parking brake. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Releases the brake parachute after landing, and drops it again (jets that have one).

Opens or closes the cockpit canopy. Open it on the ground or to bail out, close it before take-off. With a separate open and close command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Opens the cockpit canopy, on the ground or before you bail out. With a separate open and close command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Closes the cockpit canopy before take-off. With a separate open and close command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Opens or closes the cockpit side window, for example for a better view while taxiing. With a separate open and close command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Switches the landing lights on or off, to see the runway at night. Needed for night flights.
Switches the navigation (position) lights on or off, so others see you at night. Needed for night flights.
Steps through the cockpit lighting modes, to read the instruments at night. Needed for night flights.
Switches the formation lights on or off, so your wingmen see you at night. Needed for night flights.
Switches the aircraft's own autopilot on or off (aircraft that have one), which holds course and height. Only in aircraft with their own autopilot (mostly bombers and transports).
Switches the heading (yaw) channel of the aircraft autopilot on or off. Only in aircraft with their own autopilot (mostly bombers and transports).
Switches the pitch channel of the aircraft autopilot on or off. Only in aircraft with their own autopilot (mostly bombers and transports).
Switches the roll channel of the aircraft autopilot on or off. Only in aircraft with their own autopilot (mostly bombers and transports).
Turns the heading the autopilot holds a step to the left. Only in aircraft with their own autopilot (mostly bombers and transports).
Turns the heading the autopilot holds a step to the right. Only in aircraft with their own autopilot (mostly bombers and transports).
Sets the pitch the autopilot holds with an axis. Only in aircraft with their own autopilot (mostly bombers and transports).
Raises the pitch the autopilot holds a step. Only in aircraft with their own autopilot (mostly bombers and transports).
Lowers the pitch the autopilot holds a step. Only in aircraft with their own autopilot (mostly bombers and transports).
Sets the autopilot trim back to neutral. Only in aircraft with their own autopilot (mostly bombers and transports).
Turns the radio receiver volume down when the radio chatter is too loud.
Turns the radio receiver volume up when you cannot hear the radio.
Tunes the radio compass to the nearest active beacon, for navigation home.
Leaves the aircraft: by parachute in the air, or climbs out on the ground.
Lets the game handle propeller pitch, mixture and supercharger for you.
Lets the game open and close the radiators and cowl shutters for you to keep the engine cool. Watch the engine temperature: open more when it gets hot, close to go faster.
Keeps the engine from over-revving by limiting the throttle automatically.
Starts the engine start-up sequence, or stops the engine. Usually the first button you press in a mission.
Fires the ignition of the engines during start-up.
Sets the engine power. Put it on the throttle lever of your device.
Sets the fuel/air mixture: rich for take-off and combat, leaner at height to save fuel.
Switches the supercharger stage, for full power at different heights.
Switches the supercharger to the higher gear, used as you climb.
Switches the supercharger to the lower gear, used lower down.
Sets the turbocharger with an axis, for power at height.
Switches emergency power on or off for a short burst of extra power.
Switches emergency power on. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Switches emergency power off. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Sets the propeller pitch (engine RPM): high RPM for take-off and combat, lower to cruise.
Switches the propeller pitch control between manual and automatic, where the aircraft has both.
Moves the propeller to a coarser (higher) pitch, which lowers the RPM; electric propellers.
Moves the propeller to a finer (lower) pitch, which raises the RPM; electric propellers.
Feathers the propeller of a dead engine to cut its drag, or unfeathers it again.
Feathers the propeller, which stops a dead engine from windmilling and cuts its drag. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Unfeathers the propeller again, for example to restart the engine. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Opens and closes the oil radiator with an axis: more open cools better but slows you down. Watch the engine temperature: open more when it gets hot, close to go faster.
Switches the oil radiator between manual and automatic control. Watch the engine temperature: open more when it gets hot, close to go faster.
Opens the oil radiator with the servo. With a separate open and close command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Closes the oil radiator with the servo. With a separate open and close command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Opens and closes the coolant radiator with an axis: more open cools better but slows you down. Watch the engine temperature: open more when it gets hot, close to go faster.
Switches the coolant radiator between manual and automatic control. Watch the engine temperature: open more when it gets hot, close to go faster.
Opens the coolant radiator with the servo. With a separate open and close command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Closes the coolant radiator with the servo. With a separate open and close command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Opens and closes the cowl shutters in front of the engine with an axis, to control engine temperature. Watch the engine temperature: open more when it gets hot, close to go faster.
Opens and closes the cowl flaps behind the engine with an axis, to control engine temperature. Watch the engine temperature: open more when it gets hot, close to go faster.
Links the propeller RPM to the throttle lever, so one lever sets both.
Links the turbocharger to the throttle lever, so one lever sets both.
Fires the rocket boosters for extra thrust, for example on a short take-off.
Drops the burnt-out rocket boosters after take-off, to lose their weight and drag.
Picks the next fuel valve, which "Fuel valve: switch" then turns.
Turns the fuel valve you picked, to feed the engine from another tank.
Picks the next fuel pump switch, which "Fuel pump: switch" then flips.
Flips the fuel pump switch you picked with "Fuel pump: pick next".
Dumps fuel overboard, to lose weight before an emergency landing.
Switches the fuel gauge to show another tank, to see how much fuel is left where.
Starts or stops refuelling while you stand in the service area of an airfield.
Fires all fixed guns at once. Put it on the trigger of your stick.
Fires gun group 1 only (for example only machine guns or only cannons), to save the heavy ammunition.
Fires gun group 2 only (for example only machine guns or only cannons), to save the heavy ammunition.
Fires gun group 3 only (for example only machine guns or only cannons), to save the heavy ammunition.
Looks through the bomb sight for level bombing. Press again to go back to the cockpit. Set it on the way to the target, before the bomb run.

column2: Lean to the gunsight / dive sight
column4: Moves your head to the gunsight, or to the dive bombing sight where the aircraft has one, for precise aiming.
Changes which bombs are dropped and how many at once. Set it on the way to the target, before the bomb run.
Changes the time between bombs dropped in a salvo. Set it on the way to the target, before the bomb run.
Drops bombs (or releases smoke where loaded). Put it on a stick button. Set it on the way to the target, before the bomb run.
Changes how many rockets fire per press: one by one, in pairs or all.
Fires rockets at the target in front of you. Put it on a stick button.
Drops all external stores without arming them, to get light and fast.
Opens or closes the bomb bay doors; open them before you drop. Set it on the way to the target, before the bomb run.
Opens the bomb bay doors. With a separate open and close command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Closes the bomb bay doors. With a separate open and close command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Reloads or recharges the guns after a jam, where the aircraft allows it.
Puts away the flare pistol or handgun. Flares signal to others (for example before landing); you rarely need this in a fight.
Takes the flare pistol with a red flare. Flares signal to others (for example before landing); you rarely need this in a fight.
Takes the flare pistol with a green flare. Flares signal to others (for example before landing); you rarely need this in a fight.
Takes the flare pistol with a white flare. Flares signal to others (for example before landing); you rarely need this in a fight.
Takes your handgun. Flares signal to others (for example before landing); you rarely need this in a fight.
Takes the binoculars, to look far. Flares signal to others (for example before landing); you rarely need this in a fight.
Fires the flare pistol or personal weapon you hold. Flares signal to others (for example before landing); you rarely need this in a fight.
Moves you from the pilot seat to a gunner position and back, to defend against a fighter behind you.
Moves the gunner to another gun position of the turret.
Goes back to your default crew position (normally the pilot seat).
Moves you straight to crew position 1 (pilot, gunner or bombardier, depending on the aircraft).
Moves you straight to crew position 2 (pilot, gunner or bombardier, depending on the aircraft).
Moves you straight to crew position 3 (pilot, gunner or bombardier, depending on the aircraft).
Moves you straight to crew position 4 (pilot, gunner or bombardier, depending on the aircraft).
Moves you straight to crew position 5 (pilot, gunner or bombardier, depending on the aircraft).
Moves you straight to crew position 6 (pilot, gunner or bombardier, depending on the aircraft).
Moves you straight to crew position 7 (pilot, gunner or bombardier, depending on the aircraft).
Moves you straight to crew position 8 (pilot, gunner or bombardier, depending on the aircraft).
Moves you straight to crew position 9 (pilot, gunner or bombardier, depending on the aircraft).
Takes control of the turret gun at your position, or hands it back to the AI gunner.
Moves your eye to the gunsight of the turret you control, for aimed fire.
Fires the guns of the turret you control. Put it on the trigger when you fly as a gunner.
Fires the second weapon of the turret or vehicle you control.
Reloads the turret gun you control when its magazine is empty.
Swings the dark filter in front of the gunsight, for flying towards the sun. Set it before an attack so the sight shows where your rounds go.
Moves the gunsight to its other position (for example folded away). Set it before an attack so the sight shows where your rounds go.
Switches the gunsight mode (for example gyro or fixed reticle). Set it before an attack so the sight shows where your rounds go.
Sets the target range on the gunsight with an axis, so the gyro sight leads correctly. Set it before an attack so the sight shows where your rounds go.
Sets the wingspan of the target on the gunsight with an axis, so the sight can measure the range. Set it before an attack so the sight shows where your rounds go.
Sets the gunsight adjustments back to their defaults. Set it before an attack so the sight shows where your rounds go.
Turns the wind direction set on the bomb sight to the left.
Turns the wind direction set on the bomb sight to the right.
Tilts the gunsight with an axis. Set it before an attack so the sight shows where your rounds go.
Sets the wind speed on the gunsight with an axis. Set it before an attack so the sight shows where your rounds go.
Cages the gunsight (locks the reticle in the middle). Set it before an attack so the sight shows where your rounds go.
Changes the ammunition type of the gun you control, for example armour-piercing against tanks.
Lets your AI gunners shoot at any enemy in range. Used in aircraft with AI gunners (bombers, attack aircraft).
Your AI gunners only shoot back at enemies that attack you. Used in aircraft with AI gunners (bombers, attack aircraft).
Your AI gunners stop shooting. Used in aircraft with AI gunners (bombers, attack aircraft).
Your AI gunners stop firing the heavy weapons and keep the machine guns. Used in aircraft with AI gunners (bombers, attack aircraft).
Your AI gunners also shoot at balloons. Used in aircraft with AI gunners (bombers, attack aircraft).
Your AI gunners also shoot at ground targets. Used in aircraft with AI gunners (bombers, attack aircraft).
Your AI gunners open fire only at short range (saves ammunition, better hits). Used in aircraft with AI gunners (bombers, attack aircraft).
Your AI gunners open fire at normal range. Used in aircraft with AI gunners (bombers, attack aircraft).
Your AI gunners open fire already at long range. Used in aircraft with AI gunners (bombers, attack aircraft).
Starts or stops rearming while you stand in the service area of an airfield.
Your pilot signals to move on. Only for show (others see it in multiplayer); it does not change the flight.
Your pilot signals that it is enough. Only for show (others see it in multiplayer); it does not change the flight.
Your pilot raises a hand. Only for show (others see it in multiplayer); it does not change the flight.
Your pilot signals to go around. Only for show (others see it in multiplayer); it does not change the flight.
Your pilot points ahead. Only for show (others see it in multiplayer); it does not change the flight.
Your pilot signals to cancel the task. Only for show (others see it in multiplayer); it does not change the flight.
Your pilot salutes, a gesture the other players see. Only for show (others see it in multiplayer); it does not change the flight.
Your pilot offers a handshake. Only for show (others see it in multiplayer); it does not change the flight.
Your pilot shows a thumbs up. Only for show (others see it in multiplayer); it does not change the flight.
Sets the engine power of a ground vehicle with an axis. Only when you drive or crew a ground vehicle.
Steers a ground vehicle left and right with an axis. Only when you drive or crew a ground vehicle.
Shifts the vehicle gearbox one gear up. Only when you drive or crew a ground vehicle.
Shifts the vehicle gearbox one gear down. Only when you drive or crew a ground vehicle.
Switches the master arm on or off; the weapons only fire when it is on. Set it before an attack so the sight shows where your rounds go.
Turns the turret gun you control left and right directly with an axis (instead of the mouse).
Raises and lowers the turret gun you control directly with an axis (instead of the mouse).
Aims a turret up and down with the mouse. Leave it on the mouse; for an axis use "Turret: aim up/down".
Aims a turret left and right with the mouse. Leave it on the mouse; for an axis use "Turret: aim left/right".
In the game's Mouse control mode, moving the mouse up and down sets where the aircraft flies; the game steers it there. Leave it on the mouse; for a device axis use "Pitch".
In the game's Mouse control mode, moving the mouse left and right sets where the aircraft flies; the game steers it there. Leave it on the mouse; for a device axis use "Roll" and "Yaw".
In Mouse control mode, with the right mouse button held, the mouse looks up and down without changing the flight direction.
In Mouse control mode, with the right mouse button held, the mouse looks left and right without changing the flight direction.
Starts or stops the engine of the vehicle. Only when you drive or crew a ground vehicle.
Brakes the ground vehicle you drive (the game gives this one no name; vc = vehicle control). Only when you drive or crew a ground vehicle.
Switches to the far camera behind you in Mouse control mode (the mode where the mouse steers).
Switches to the close camera in Mouse control mode (the mode where the mouse steers). With a separate open and close command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
A key for the special mission panels (air reconnaissance target list, photo reconnaissance, artillery spotting): picks entry 1 or marks/photographs, as the panel shows. Only needed in such missions.
A key for the special mission panels (air reconnaissance target list, photo reconnaissance, artillery spotting): picks entry 2 or marks/photographs, as the panel shows. Only needed in such missions.
A key for the special mission panels (air reconnaissance target list, photo reconnaissance, artillery spotting): picks entry 3 or marks/photographs, as the panel shows. Only needed in such missions.
A key for the special mission panels (air reconnaissance target list, photo reconnaissance, artillery spotting): picks entry 4 or marks/photographs, as the panel shows. Only needed in such missions.
A key for the special mission panels (air reconnaissance target list, photo reconnaissance, artillery spotting): picks entry 5 or marks/photographs, as the panel shows. Only needed in such missions.
A key for the special mission panels (air reconnaissance target list, photo reconnaissance, artillery spotting): picks entry 6 or marks/photographs, as the panel shows. Only needed in such missions.
A key for the special mission panels (air reconnaissance target list, photo reconnaissance, artillery spotting): picks entry 7 or marks/photographs, as the panel shows. Only needed in such missions.
A key for the special mission panels (air reconnaissance target list, photo reconnaissance, artillery spotting): picks entry 8 or marks/photographs, as the panel shows. Only needed in such missions.
A key for the special mission panels (air reconnaissance target list, photo reconnaissance, artillery spotting): picks entry 9 or marks/photographs, as the panel shows. Only needed in such missions.
A key for the special mission panels (air reconnaissance target list, photo reconnaissance, artillery spotting): picks entry 0 or marks/photographs, as the panel shows. Only needed in such missions.
Moves the menu pointer left and right (normally the mouse). Leave it on the mouse.
Moves the menu pointer up and down (normally the mouse). Leave it on the mouse.
Scrolls lists in the menus (normally the mouse wheel).
Clicks in the menus (normally the left mouse button).
Right click in the menus (normally the right mouse button).
Middle click in the menus (normally the middle mouse button).
Opens the quick multi-function menu with the common in-game options.
Opens the systems menu with the state of the aircraft systems.
Moves the selection in the game menus right, for playing with a gamepad or device instead of the mouse.
Moves the selection in the game menus left, for playing with a gamepad or device instead of the mouse.
Moves the selection in the game menus down, for playing with a gamepad or device instead of the mouse.
Moves the selection in the game menus up, for playing with a gamepad or device instead of the mouse.
Confirms the selected menu entry (like Enter), when you use the menus with a gamepad or device.
Leaves the menu or dialog without a change (like Esc).
Runs the first extra action the current menu page offers.
Runs the second extra action the current menu page offers.
Moves the focus to the next element of the menu page. Good on a rotary or a two-way switch.
Moves the focus to the previous element of the menu page. Good on a rotary or a two-way switch.
Steps back to the previous mode of the mini-map in the HUD.
Arms or safes the bomb fuses. Armed bombs explode on impact; safe ones do not. Set it on the way to the target, before the bomb run.
Sets the brightness of the gunsight reticle with an axis. Set it before an attack so the sight shows where your rounds go.
Sets the range limit of the radar rangefinder with an axis (the id prefix rc is the radar rangefinder).
Drops the target the radar rangefinder measures, so it looks for a new one.
Switches the radar warning receiver and radar rangefinder on or off.
Orders your gunners to leave the aircraft by parachute. Used in aircraft with AI gunners (bombers, attack aircraft).
Drops the external fuel tanks, for example before a fight.
The brake of a ground vehicle. Only when you drive or crew a ground vehicle.
The clutch of a ground vehicle. Only when you drive or crew a ground vehicle.
Skips the cut-scene or video that is playing, to get into the mission faster.
Switches to the external camera on the aircraft closest to you. Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
Switches to the external camera on the ground unit closest to you. Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
Follows the bomb or rocket closest to you. Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
Steps through the larger set of cameras, one per press.
Switches between the external camera and the cockpit.
An external camera on the current object that reacts to its movements. Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
A moving camera the current object flies past. Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
In a replay: lets an automatic cameraman pick the shots.
Tilts the external camera to the right or left. Mostly for replays, screenshots and videos.
Tilts your head view to the right and left with an axis.
The computer holds the current climb or descent rate.
While a flight helper holds the aircraft, steers it into a normal right turn.
While a flight helper holds the aircraft, steers it into a normal left turn.
Lets the game manage tanks and fuel pumps for you.
Switches the cowl shutters between manual and automatic control. Watch the engine temperature: open more when it gets hot, close to go faster.
Opens the outlet cowl flaps with the servo. With a separate open and close command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Closes the outlet cowl flaps with the servo. With a separate open and close command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Drops the landing gear with the emergency system when the normal system has failed.
Extends or retracts the flaps one step per press, for take-off and landing.
Switches the taxi lights on or off. Needed for night flights.
Switches the identification (code) lights on or off. Needed for night flights.
Selects the next cockpit gauge you can operate with the gauge buttons. Use it to set gauges (clock, compass, altimeter) without the mouse.
Selects the previous cockpit gauge you can operate with the gauge buttons. Use it to set gauges (clock, compass, altimeter) without the mouse.
Selects the next control of the selected gauge. Use it to set gauges (clock, compass, altimeter) without the mouse.
Selects the previous control of the selected gauge. Use it to set gauges (clock, compass, altimeter) without the mouse.
Pushes or turns the selected cockpit control one step up. Use it to set gauges (clock, compass, altimeter) without the mouse.
Turns the selected cockpit control one step down. Use it to set gauges (clock, compass, altimeter) without the mouse.
Switches the altimeter between the airfield pressure (height above the field) and standard pressure.
Tunes the radio compass to the next beacon channel.
Tunes the radio compass to the previous beacon channel.
Fires the ejection seat (jets that have one). Use it when the aircraft is lost.
Throws the canopy away, for example before bailing out.
Walks your pilot forward when he is out of the aircraft.
Walks your pilot backward when he is out of the aircraft.
Turns your pilot right when he is out of the aircraft.
Turns your pilot left when he is out of the aircraft.
Makes your pilot run while he walks outside the aircraft.
Makes your pilot crouch while he is outside the aircraft.
Does nothing in the game; a key bound here is kept free from other commands.
Moves the selection in the game menus right and left with an axis (for example a mini stick).
Moves the selection in the game menus down and up with an axis (for example a mini stick).
Moves your head in the cockpit forward and back with an axis.
Moves your head in the cockpit up and down with an axis.
Moves your head in the cockpit right and left with an axis.
The left rudder pedal as its own axis, for pedals that report each pedal separately.
The right rudder pedal as its own axis, for pedals that report each pedal separately.
Drops the defensive grenades behind the aircraft against a chasing fighter (Il-10).
Starts the engine start-up sequence; the game runs every step for you. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Stops the engine, for example after landing. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Lets the servo control the water radiator automatically. Watch the engine temperature: open more when it gets hot, close to go faster.
Puts the water radiator under your manual control. Watch the engine temperature: open more when it gets hot, close to go faster.
Lets the servo control the oil radiator automatically. Watch the engine temperature: open more when it gets hot, close to go faster.
Puts the oil radiator under your manual control. Watch the engine temperature: open more when it gets hot, close to go faster.
Lets the servo control the cowl shutters automatically. Watch the engine temperature: open more when it gets hot, close to go faster.
Puts the cowl shutters under your manual control. Watch the engine temperature: open more when it gets hot, close to go faster.
Opens the cockpit side window. With a separate open and close command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Closes the cockpit side window. With a separate open and close command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Steps to the next cockpit lighting mode. Good on a rotary or a two-way switch.
Steps to the previous cockpit lighting mode. Good on a rotary or a two-way switch.
Switches the landing lights on. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Switches the landing lights off. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Switches the taxi lights on. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Switches the taxi lights off. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Switches the navigation lights on. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Switches the navigation lights off. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Switches the formation lights on. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Switches the formation lights off. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Switches the code lights on. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Switches the code lights off. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Switches the master arm on, so the weapons can fire. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Switches the master arm off, so the weapons cannot fire. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Switches the gunsight to its next mode. Good on a rotary or a two-way switch.
Switches the gunsight to its previous mode. Good on a rotary or a two-way switch.
Moves the gunsight to its next position. Good on a rotary or a two-way switch.
Moves the gunsight to its previous position. Good on a rotary or a two-way switch.
Swings the dark filter in front of the gunsight. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Swings the dark filter away from the gunsight. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Locks (cages) the gyro gunsight reticle in the middle. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Frees (uncages) the gyro gunsight reticle again. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Switches the radar warning receiver and radar rangefinder on. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Switches the radar warning receiver and radar rangefinder off. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Steps the bomb selector to the next setting. Good on a rotary or a two-way switch.
Steps the bomb selector to the previous setting. Good on a rotary or a two-way switch.
Steps the rocket selector to the next setting. Good on a rotary or a two-way switch.
Steps the rocket selector to the previous setting. Good on a rotary or a two-way switch.
Arms the bomb fuses. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Safes the bomb fuses so the bombs do not explode. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Sets the heading the autopilot holds with an axis. Only in aircraft with their own autopilot (mostly bombers and transports).
Switches the hydraulic aileron booster on, for lighter roll control at high speed. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Switches the hydraulic aileron booster off. With a separate on and off command a two-position switch on your device always matches the game.
Switches the stabilising flight helper on or off, which smooths your control inputs.
Moves your eye to the gunsight of the vehicle gun. Only when you drive or crew a ground vehicle.
Opens or closes the hatch of the vehicle position. Only when you drive or crew a ground vehicle.
Opens or closes the armoured vision slit. Only when you drive or crew a ground vehicle.
Lowers or raises the sun shade. Only when you drive or crew a ground vehicle.
Steps through the interior lights: instruments, flood, off. Only when you drive or crew a ground vehicle.
Switches the vehicle headlights on or off. Only when you drive or crew a ground vehicle.
Sounds the horn. Only when you drive or crew a ground vehicle.
Takes control of the vehicle turret, or hands it back. Only when you drive or crew a ground vehicle.
Reloads the machine gun. Only when you drive or crew a ground vehicle.
Fires the main gun of the vehicle. Only when you drive or crew a ground vehicle.
Sets the compass director or turn signal to the left.
Sets the compass director or turn signal to the right.
Switches the fuel gauge of the vehicle to another tank.
Shows the fuel pump pressure on the vehicle fuel gauge.
Lowers or raises the vehicle supports (stabilisers) for firing.
Moves the vehicle gun sight up and down with an axis. Only when you drive or crew a ground vehicle.
Moves the vehicle gun sight sideways with an axis. Only when you drive or crew a ground vehicle.
Puts the vehicle gun sight back to the middle. Only when you drive or crew a ground vehicle.
Sets the sideways correction of the vehicle gun sight with an axis. Only when you drive or crew a ground vehicle.
